solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perhaps school member only returning a musical instrument

parts.note: a bass is a fish, and fish swim in schools, so one fish of a school could be a bass

indicators.note: returning tells us to read the word for 'only' backwards

parts.note: only means but, as in 'there was but one'

explanation.surface: A pupil coming back to school carrying a single instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school member' looks like a pupil, but a school here is a shoal of fish. 'returning' turns BUT into TUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument with the lowest pitch of its family, so it is one example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Busybody keeps relative half- cut with wine

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a busy bee is a byword for someone always active, so a busybody here is a bee

indicators.note: half cut means only the first half of the relative's word is kept

parts.note: an auntie is a relative

explanation.surface: A nosy person keeps a tipsy relative company over some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half- cut' reads as slang for tipsy, but here it keeps only the first half of the relative's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Burgundy town whose name is given to the red and white wines made around it.

clue.text: Crux of plot appears in similar opera

indicators.note: appears in places the central letters inside the word for 'similar'

parts.note: similar means the same

indicators.note: the crux is the heart of something, so take the middle letters of plot

explanation.surface: The main point of a story turns up in a comparable opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss wrote a one-act work with this title, based on Oscar Wilde's play about Herod's stepdaughter.

clue.text: Landscape painter touring Britain tracks course in Scotland

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the painter's name surrounds the letter for Britain

parts.note: J. M. W. Turner was a great English landscape painter
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of tracks

explanation.surface: A landscape artist travels Britain following tracks to a Scottish venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tracks' stands for railway. The answer is a famous golf links on the Ayrshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A championship golf links on Scotland's west coast that has hosted the Open, so it is a Scottish course.

clue.text: Hefty fare that man contested at Waterloo after gripe

indicators.note: after tells us the general's name follows the word for gripe

parts.note: a beef is a complaint or gripe
the Duke of Wellington fought and beat Napoleon at Waterloo in 1815

explanation.surface: A big meal eaten by the victor of Waterloo after a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillet of meat wrapped in pastry is a rich, substantial dish, so it is heavy food.

clue.text: Writer, when shaving, coins fundamental word in Italian

indicators.note: shaving takes a little off the end, so the coins lose their last letter

parts.note: pence are British coins
il, the Italian word for 'the', is one of the most basic words in that language

explanation.surface: A writer shaving off bits of coins while learning Italian basics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaving' trims PENCE to PENC.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphite stick in a wooden case is something you write with, so it is a writer.

clue.text: Land near the houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: Ground close to some homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth means soil or the ground, the dry part of the world, so it is a synonym of land.

clue.text: Revolutionary spirit attracts two angelic-looking people

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary

indicators.note: attracts means draws in, so the spirit holds the prefix for two

parts.note: rum is a spirit
bi- is the prefix for two

explanation.surface: A rebel spirit draws a pair of sweet-faced figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of cherub, used for chubby, innocent-faced children who look like painted angels.

clue.text: Academic's landlord extended after vacation

parts.note: a letter is someone who lets property, a landlord

indicators.note: vacating empties a word, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A lecturer's landlord lengthened the lease after the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday, but it empties 'extended' to ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettered means learned or well read, so it describes an academic, scholarly person.

clue.text: Chicken dish Leonard cooked with ginger

indicators.note: cooked means altered or prepared, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ginger as a hair colour means red

explanation.surface: A poultry meal that Leonard prepared with ginger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' mixes DISH and LEONARD into RHODEISLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of domestic fowl named after the American state, so it is a kind of chicken.

clue.text: In full gear suffering after attending opening of library

indicators.note: after means the mixed letters follow the earlier pieces

parts.note: attending means at, as in at a meeting

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
suffering means damaged, so the letters of gear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fully kitted out and in pain after going to the library's opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' turns GEAR into ARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: At large can mean in full or at length, as in discussing a matter at large.

clue.text: Most complicated threads to embroider

indicators.note: embroidering works fabric into new patterns, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The trickiest threads to stitch into a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardest means most difficult, the superlative of hard in its sense of tricky or complicated.

clue.text: Desert bar as one male enters rolling about

indicators.note: rolling about turns the whole assembly round so it reads backwards
enters means goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: to ban is to bar
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A barred zone a man stumbles into while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: I and M go inside BAN to make BIMAN; 'rolling about' turns it to NAMIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal desert running along the Atlantic coast of Namibia and Angola.

clue.text: Novelist who grasps poetry with practice

indicators.note: grasps means holds, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: an ode is a poem, a piece of poetry
use means custom or practice

explanation.surface: A writer who gets the hang of verse through rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' looks like a link word, but it gives its own letters around ODE.
explanation.definitionFit: P. G. Wodehouse wrote the comic Jeeves and Wooster novels, so he is a novelist.

clue.text: Talented creator, born for hairdressing

parts.note: brilliant means very talented
the setter is the creator of the puzzle, who calls themself I
ne is short for nee, meaning born

explanation.surface: A gifted maker born to style hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's creator is the setter, who speaks as I; NE is the French-derived nee, born.
explanation.definitionFit: An oily dressing used to make hair glossy, so it is a hairdressing product.

clue.text: Composer Michael wanted to embrace aristocrat — he almost reaches

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold around, so the composer's name surrounds the noble title

parts.note: Michael Nyman is the English composer of The Piano score
an earl is an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A composer longed to hug a nobleman who kept just missing out.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who repeatedly comes close to success without quite achieving it is called this, so he almost reaches the top.

clue.text: Dotty taking alcoholic drink in outskirts of Stroud

indicators.note: in places the drink between the outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a tipple is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone a bit mad having a drink on the edge of a Gloucestershire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like crazy, but it means covered in dots. Stroud is a town in Gloucestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippled means marked with many small dots, so it is a literal sense of dotty.

clue.text: River boat, one with elite soldiers

parts.note: an ark is a boat, like Noah's
an means one, as in an apple
the SAS is the British Army's elite Special Air Service

explanation.surface: A river craft with a single crack trooper aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A major tributary of the Mississippi flowing through four US states, so it is a river.

clue.text: Film director using uncut material by Shakespeare, good for opening

parts.note: terry is a fabric with uncut loops of pile, used for towels

indicators.note: for opening means the letter for good takes the place of the first letter

parts.note: William was Shakespeare's first name

explanation.surface: A director working with fabric and Shakespeare, keeping goodness for the opening scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for opening' puts G in place of the W at the start of WILLIAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry Gilliam, of Monty Python, made films such as Brazil and Twelve Monkeys, so he is a film director.

clue.text: Father having to cough up a tropical fruit

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to cough up is to pay

explanation.surface: Dad has to spend money on an exotic fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, orange-fleshed fruit of the pawpaw tree grown in hot climates, so it is a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Attempt to penetrate wood to uproot evergreen shrub

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up roots lifts the whole assembly so it reads from the bottom upward
to penetrate means to go inside the wood's name

parts.note: elm is a wood
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to get into a wood to dig up a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to uproot' reads as digging out, but in a down entry it means the assembly reads upward, giving ELTRYM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant shrub with glossy leaves that stay all year, so it is an evergreen bush.

clue.text: Game bird training horse to turn after limb originally injured

indicators.note: after says the horse's letters follow the limb and its initial

parts.note: PT is physical training
an arm is a limb

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the next word
to turn means the word for horse is read backwards

parts.note: a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: Training a horse to turn round after a leg injury, with a bird nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' makes NAG into GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouse of mountain and Arctic regions that is shot for sport, so it is a game bird.

clue.text: Drive doctor to river

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Take the doctor down to the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a command, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is to travel by car, so it means to drive.

clue.text: Line delineates a piece of field abounding with trees

indicators.note: to delineate is to trace an outline around, so the line encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a ley is a line, as in ley lines

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A line marks out part of a field full of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: A and F go inside LEY. Ley lines are supposed lines linking ancient sites.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafy describes a place with plenty of foliage and trees, such as a leafy suburb.

clue.text: Stars accepted arrangement of host nation

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the constellation holds the mixed letters

parts.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

indicators.note: arrangement of means the letters of host are reordered

explanation.surface: Celebrities agree to the plans of a hosting country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like celebrities, but it is the constellation; 'arrangement of' makes HOST into SOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A small kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, so it is a nation.

clue.text: Academy paintings captivate minister for defence

indicators.note: captivate means hold captive, so the pieces surround the minister

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy
art means paintings
an MP, member of parliament, can be a minister

explanation.surface: Royal Academy pictures charm the defence secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Academy is London's leading art institution; 'captivate' means the minister is held captive inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive wall or earth bank around a fort, so it is a defence.

clue.text: Fancy gentleman diving into British river

indicators.note: diving into means going inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
sir is the title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman plunges into a river in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is a noun here, a liking.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a wish or longing, so it is a synonym of desire.

clue.text: Toothless thing in rubbish eaten by garden creature ultimately

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside the other pieces

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Something without teeth in a rubbish heap gets eaten by a garden creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creature ultimately' adds an E after the garden before the rubbish is swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: An edentate is a mammal lacking front teeth, such as a sloth or anteater, so it is a toothless thing.
